checks: The hypotheses keep a common ball in each original positive fiber. At each b below inradius, distance-to-boundary coarea gives the integral of inner parallel surface area. The distance has gradient norm one almost everywhere in the interior, and level boundaries at submaximal b coincide with the inner parallel boundaries. The inball homothety gives Hausdorff continuity at these levels, so the derivative with respect to b is the stated surface area. Counting measure gives two in dimension one.

For b_z=delta_t exp(h+v·(z-j)), the eroded fibers approach the original ones uniformly on compact parameter sets. Surface area continuity then gives C^1 convergence of the scaled map, with Jacobian term S_z exp(h+v·(z-j))q_z q_z^T.

Strict positivity of the old volume weights puts j in the relative interior. For a strictly interior target, a ball centered at that target in the relative affine span gives coercivity of the log-sum-exp difference. Positive exponential weights give positive covariance on the base span, and the q_z span the extra mass dimension, so the full Jacobian is invertible. At rank zero the scalar mass equation remains.

A contraction on a fixed small ball about the limiting root solves the exact finite-t mass and first base moment equations. The same local argument for nearby targets and finite cover gives the compact-interior uniformity. The old centered first moment is zero and the prescribed removals cancel the added first base moment exactly. A proper exposed face gives the stated obstruction to cheaper cancellation for additions supported entirely there.
